title: POST callback requires redirect_uri but never uses it

evidence.quote:
class OAuthCallbackRequest(BaseModel):
    """OAuth callback request body."""

    code: str
    redirect_uri: str
    state: str

reasoning: The request schema makes redirect_uri mandatory, but the route ignores body.redirect_uri entirely. That creates a misleading OpenAPI/API contract: clients must send a value that cannot affect behavior, and a mismatched value is not rejected by this layer. For an OAuth callback contract this is especially confusing because redirect_uri is normally part of the token exchange inputs.
reproduction: Call POST /oauth/callback with any redirect_uri value; the route only passes code and state to exchange_code_with_callback, so the supplied redirect_uri is indistinguishable from a correct one at the handler boundary.
recommendation: Either remove redirect_uri from OAuthCallbackRequest if the callback intentionally uses only server-stored pending OAuth state, or validate/use it explicitly so the handler rejects values that do not match the pending OAuth flow.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and the repository search found only service-level newsletter tests, not route tests for POST /oauth/callback or its request contract.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FastAPI route test for POST /api/newsletters/oauth/callback that sends a mismatched redirect_uri and asserts the intended behavior: either validation fails, or redirect_uri is no longer part of the accepted request schema.
minimumFixScope: app/api/newsletters.py request model and oauth_callback_post handler; possibly the newsletter service if matching against stored redirect_uri is implemented there.
